exposure: Demographic and clinical factors (e.g., CRP, platelet counts, inotropic medication, intubation, positive blood cultures within 24h of diagnosis, abdominal circumference at birth)
Nutrition at NEC onset (e.g., maternal milk intake, human milk fortifiers)
outcome: Surgical NEC (progression to surgery or death)
cohort: The study participants were 216 infants diagnosed with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) between 2010 and 2020.
finding: Elevated CRP, rapidly decreasing platelet counts, inotropic medication, intubation, positive blood cultures, and higher abdominal circumferences at birth were associated with progression to surgical NEC, while maternal milk intake and human milk fortifiers were associated with medical NEC.
